```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(psych)
library(gt)
library(gtsummary)
library(sjPlot)
library(ggsankey)
library(ggpubr)
library(pscl)

# Correlation Matrix function
corstars_descriptives <-function(x, method=c("pearson", "spearman"), removeTriangle=c("upper", "lower"),
                     result=c("none", "html", "latex"), descriptives =c("basic")){
    #Compute correlation matrix
    require(Hmisc)
    require(xtable)
    x <- as.matrix(x)
    correlation_matrix<-rcorr(x, type=method[1])
    R <- correlation_matrix$r # Matrix of correlation coeficients
    p <- correlation_matrix$P # Matrix of p-value 
    
    ## Define notions for significance levels; spacing is important.
    mystars <- ifelse(p < .001, "*** ", ifelse(p < .01, "**  ", ifelse(p < .05, "*   ", "    ")))
    
    ## trunctuate the correlation matrix to two decimal
    R <- format(round(cbind(rep(-1.11, ncol(x)), R), 2))[,-1]
    
    ## build a new matrix that includes the correlations with their apropriate stars
    Rnew <- matrix(paste(R, mystars, sep=""), ncol=ncol(x))
    diag(Rnew) <- paste(diag(R), " ", sep="")
    rownames(Rnew) <- colnames(x)
    colnames(Rnew) <- paste(colnames(x), "", sep="")
    
    ## remove upper triangle of correlation matrix
    if(removeTriangle[1]=="upper"){
      Rnew <- as.matrix(Rnew)
      Rnew[upper.tri(Rnew, diag = TRUE)] <- ""
      Rnew <- as.data.frame(Rnew)
    }
    
    ## remove lower triangle of correlation matrix
    else if(removeTriangle[1]=="lower"){
      Rnew <- as.matrix(Rnew)
      Rnew[lower.tri(Rnew, diag = TRUE)] <- ""
      Rnew <- as.data.frame(Rnew)
    }
    
    ## remove last column or 
    Rnew <- cbind(Rnew[1:length(Rnew)]) %>% t()

    ## Create descriptives
    ###basic: only Mean & SD
    if(descriptives[1] == "basic"){
      Demo <- psych::describe(x, skew = F, ranges = T) %>% round(digits = 2)
      Demo <- as.data.frame(Demo) %>% 
        mutate(min.dup = min, max.dup = max ) %>%
        unite(col = Range, min.dup, max.dup, sep = " - ")
      rownames(Demo) <- colnames(x)
      Demo <- t(Demo)
      Demo <- as.data.frame(Demo[c("mean","sd","Range"),])
      rownames(Demo) <- c("Mean", "SD", "Range")        
    }
    
    ### skew: Mean, SD, Skew, Kurtosis
    else if(descriptives[1] == "skew"){
      Demo <- psych::describe(x, skew = T, ranges = T) %>% round(digits = 2)
      Demo <- as.data.frame(Demo) %>% 
        mutate(min.dup = min, max.dup = max ) %>%
        unite(col = Range, min.dup, max.dup, sep = " - ")
      rownames(Demo) <- colnames(x)
      Demo <- t(Demo)
      Demo <- as.data.frame(Demo[c("mean","sd","Range", "skew", "kurtosis"),])
      rownames(Demo) <- c("Mean", "SD", "Range", "Skew", "Kurtosis") 
             
    }
    
    
    ## Bind descriptives
    Rnew <- as.data.frame(
      rbind(
      Rnew, 
      Demo
      )
    )
    
    ## return the correlation matrix
    if (result[1]=="none") return(Rnew)
    else{
      if(result[1]=="html") print(xtable(Rnew), type="html")
      else print(xtable(Rnew), type="latex") 
    }
    
} 

setwd("directory/")
```

# Aims:
Considering the following:
1.	“Psychological predictors of vaping uptake/susceptibility over time. Grace recently published a cross-sectional paper linking psychological variables to vaping susceptibility in young adults ages 18 - 25. Personality traits (such as conscientiousness, Openness/Intellect) and mental health variables (higher Anxiety) predicted self-reported vaping and self-rated likelihood of trying vaping in the future. But it would be more informative to see to what extent these psychological variables forward predict the likelihood / uptake of vaping over time particularly using longitudinal data. Might need to stratify by age or only focus on young adults.


Breaking this down. Aim is to longitudinally explore the role of psychological variables on uptake of vaping.

```{r}
#Shift data to factors

  mutate(

    age_group.T12 = dplyr::case_when(

      Age.T12 >= 25 & Age.T12 < 35 ~ "26-35",
      Age.T12 >= 35 & Age.T12 < 45 ~ "36-45",

    age_group.T11 = dplyr::case_when(
      Age.T11 < 18           ~ "<18",

    ),
    age_group.T10 = dplyr::case_when(
      Age.T10 < 18           ~ "<18",

      Age.T10 >= 25 & Age.T10 < 35 ~ "26-35",
      Age.T10 >= 35 & Age.T10 < 45 ~ "36-45",
      Age.T10 >= 45             ~ "45+"
    ),
    # Convert to factor
    #age_group.T12 = factor(age_group.T12, level = c("<18", "19-25","26-35", "36-45", "45+")),
    #age_group.T11 = factor(age_group.T12, level = c("<18", "19-25","26-35", "36-45", "45+")),
    #age_group.T10 = factor(age_group.T10, level = c("<18", "19-25","26-35", "36-45", "45+")),
    Gender.T12 = factor(Gender.T12, level = c(0,1)),
    Gender.T11 = factor(Gender.T11, level = c(0,1)),
    Gender.T10 = factor(Gender.T10, level = c(0,1)),
```

# Visualisations

## Non-current user T10 to... (Unadjusted for missing data)

```{r}
sankey.data.simplified <- vap_data %>%
  mutate(
    T10 = case_when(Smoker.T10 == 0 & Vaper.T10 == 0 ~ "Non-User",
                    is.na(Smoker.T10) | is.na(Vaper.T10) ~ "No Vaping Data T10"),
    T11 = case_when(Smoker.T11 == 0 & Vaper.T11 == 1 ~ "Vaper Only T11",
                    Smoker.T11 == 1 & Vaper.T11 == 0 ~ "Smoker Only T11",
                    Smoker.T11 == 1 & Vaper.T11 == 1 ~ "Dual Use T11",
                    Smoker.T11 == 0 & Vaper.T11 == 0 ~ "Non-User T11",
                    is.na(Smoker.T11) | is.na(Vaper.T11) ~ "No Vaping Data T11"),
    T12 = case_when(Smoker.T12 == 0 & Vaper.T12 == 1 ~ "Vaper Only T12",
                    Smoker.T12 == 1 & Vaper.T12 == 0 ~ "Smoker Only T12",
                    Smoker.T12 == 1 & Vaper.T12 == 1 ~ "Dual User T11",
                    Smoker.T12 == 0 & Vaper.T12 == 0 ~ "Non-User T12",
                    is.na(Smoker.T12) | is.na(Vaper.T12) ~ "No Vaping Data T12")
    ) %>%
  select(T10, T11, T12)
    
sankey.long <- sankey.data.simplified %>%
  filter(T10 != is.na(T10)) %>%
  filter(T11 != is.na(T11)) %>%
  filter(T12 != is.na(T12)) %>%
  make_long(T10, T11, T12) 

sank <- sankey.long %>%
  group_by(node) %>%
  count()

sankey.mod <- merge(sankey.long, sank, by.x = 'node', by.y = 'node', all.x = TRUE)

ggplot(sankey.mod, aes(x = x, next_x = next_x, node = node, next_node = next_node, label = paste0(node, "\n (n = ", n, ")"), fill = factor(node))) +
  geom_sankey(flow.alpha = .5,
              node.color = 2) +
  geom_sankey_label(size = 3, color = "white", fill = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "inferno", alpha = .5) +
  theme_sankey(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x = element_blank())

```

# Modelling - Overall influence of personality on Vaping

## Cross Sectional Models

At the first step, let's determine whether personality characteristics are predicting vaping (yes/no) at each time point.

### T10
```{r}
t10.cross <- glm(Vaper.T10 ~ Extro + Neuro + Consc + Agree + Openn + Mental.Health + Self.Control +
              #Controlling for:
              Gender + Age + SES + Ethnicity, 
              data = vap_data.per %>%
                rename(Extro = Extro.T10,
                       Neuro = Neuro.T10,
                       Consc = Consc.T10,
                       Agree = Agree.T10,
                       Openn = Openn.T10,
                       Mental.Health = T10.KESSLER6,
                       Self.Control = T10.SELF.CONTROL,
                       Gender = Gender.T10,
                       Age = Age.T10,
                       SES = NZDep.2018.T10,
                       Ethnicity = EthnicCats.T10),
              family = "binomial") 

```

## Longitudinal Model: RQ: Is there an overall effect of personality on vaping?

```{r}
#Wrangle: Convert to long format.
vap_data.per <- vap_data.per %>% rename(ID = "...1")

vap.long <- vap_data.per %>%
  select(
    ID, Vaper.T10, Vaper.T11, Vaper.T12
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Vaper.T10, Vaper.T11, Vaper.T12),
    names_to = "Time",
    names_prefix = "Vaper.T",
    values_to = "Vaper"
  ) 

extro.long <- vap_data.per %>%
  select(
    ID, Extro.T10, Extro.T11, Extro.T12
  ) %>%
```

# Modelling: Predicting transition to vaping - Wrangling

```{r}
#Wrangle to insert dummy variables to code for behaviours
vap_data.per <- vap_data.per %>%
  mutate(
    #Non-User 0, Vaper Only 1, Smoker Only 2, Dual User 3
    Behaviour.T10 = case_when(
      Vaper.T10 == 0 & Smoker.T10 == 0 ~ 0,
      Vaper.T10 == 1 & Smoker.T10 == 0 ~ 1,
      Vaper.T10 == 0 & Smoker.T10 == 1 ~ 2,
      Vaper.T10 == 1 & Smoker.T10 == 1 ~ 3),
    Behaviour.T11 = case_when(
      Vaper.T11 == 0 & Smoker.T11 == 0 ~ 0,
      Vaper.T11 == 1 & Smoker.T11 == 0 ~ 1,
      Vaper.T11 == 0 & Smoker.T11 == 1 ~ 2,
      Vaper.T11 == 1 & Smoker.T11 == 1 ~ 3),
    Behaviour.T12 = case_when(
      Vaper.T12 == 0 & Smoker.T12 == 0 ~ 0,
      Vaper.T12 == 1 & Smoker.T12 == 0 ~ 1,
      Vaper.T12 == 0 & Smoker.T12 == 1 ~ 2,
      Vaper.T12 == 1 & Smoker.T12 == 1 ~ 3)
  )

vap.corr <- vap_data.per %>%
            rename(Mental.Health.T10 = T10.KESSLER6,
                   Self.Control.T10 = T10.SELF.CONTROL,
                   Mental.Health.T11 = T11.KESSLER6,
                   Self.Control.T11 = T11.SELF.CONTROL,
                   Mental.Health.T12 = T12.KESSLER6,
                   Self.Control.T12 = T12.SELF.CONTROL,
                   Ethnicity.T10 = EthnicCats.T10, 
                   Ethnicity.T11 = EthnicCats.T11, 
                   Ethnicity.T12 = EthnicCats.T12,
                   SES.T10 = NZDep.2018.T10,
                   SES.T11 = NZDep.2018.T11, 
                   SES.T12 = NZDep.2018.T12) %>%
            select(Smoker.T12, Smoker.T11, Smoker.T10,
                   Vaper.T12, Vaper.T11, Vaper.T10,
                   #Personality t-1
                   Extro.T10, Extro.T11, Extro.T12,
                   Neuro.T10, Neuro.T11, Neuro.T12,
                   Consc.T10, Consc.T11, Consc.T12,
                   Agree.T10, Agree.T11, Agree.T12,
                   Openn.T10, Openn.T11, Openn.T12,
                   #MH & SC
                   Mental.Health.T10, Mental.Health.T11, Mental.Health.T12,
                   Self.Control.T10, Self.Control.T11, Self.Control.T12,
                   #Covariates t
                   Gender.T10, Gender.T11, Gender.T12,
                   Age.T10, Age.T11, Age.T12,
                   Ethnicity.T10, Ethnicity.T11, Ethnicity.T12,
                   SES.T10, SES.T11, SES.T12,
                   #Other Vars
                   Behaviour.T10,
                   Behaviour.T11,
                   Behaviour.T12)

vap.corr$Smoker.T12 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Smoker.T12)


vap.corr$Vaper.T12 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Vaper.T12)
vap.corr$Vaper.T11 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Vaper.T11)
vap.corr$Vaper.T10 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Vaper.T10)

vap.corr$SES.T12 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$SES.T12)
vap.corr$SES.T11 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$SES.T11)
vap.corr$SES.T10 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$SES.T10)

vap.corr$Gender.T12 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Gender.T12)

vap.corr$Gender.T10 <- as.numeric(vap.corr$Gender.T10)

write.csv(vap.corr, file = "Vaping Data - Simple Models.csv")
```

```{r}
#Creating Transition Groups using wide data - if, all we're caring about non-user to vape
vap.transitions <- vap_data.per %>% 
  mutate(
    Transition1 = case_when(
      #NU - V = 1, NU - NV = 0
      Vaper.T10 == 0 & Smoker.T10 == 0 & Vaper.T11 == 1 & Smoker.T11 == 0 ~ "1",
      Vaper.T10 == 0 & Smoker.T10 == 0 & Vaper.T11 == 0 & Smoker.T11 == 0 ~ "0"),
    Transition2 = case_when(
      Vaper.T11 == 0 & Smoker.T11 == 0 & Vaper.T12 == 1 & Smoker.T12 == 0 ~ "1",
      Vaper.T11 == 0 & Smoker.T11 == 0 & Vaper.T12 == 0  & Smoker.T12 == 0~ "0")
  )

  select(
    ID, Transition1, Transition2
```
